producer_report.summary: docs/spec.toml now cites every BRIEF.md heading that has text under it and every dated addendum. I added 127 requirements: the Goal, Who's who, How to read, Settings, O1–O5, Running, Standards, Boundaries, Startup notes, A1–A13, S1–S7, D1–D3, Order, How I'll judge it, the Project Olympus purpose, the opening of section 4, the addenda before 2026-10-17 (including 2026-10-12 Chunking and parallel work) and those after 2026-10-24. The 2026-10-13 acceleration addendum was already cited by OLY-A-22, so I added nothing for it. The new Goal requirement OLY-B-GOAL-05 quotes "measurably faster, cheaper, and more correct". Each new requirement has verbatim quotes plus mechanism, owner and measure. Where I could not name a real mechanism I wrote `none` or said what is missing. I added 8 open questions, OQ-4 to OQ-11, each quoting both sides and none resolved. They cover non-Rust files vs "common sense", study order vs parallel, tokens vs speed, history vs brownfield, self-verification vs auditor, strangers vs agents, O2 replaced by Olympus, and trigger vs parallel loop. xtask/tests/spec.rs now reads the whole brief and fails when any heading with text, or any dated addendum, is not the first source heading of a requirement. The cutoff at 2026-10-24 and the two pinned late headings are gone. Headings with no text (the title, part and group headings, Addenda, section 6, section 9) are exempt, and a test pins that list. New negative tests remove the requirements for A6, the chunking addendum, a late addendum, Goal and "How I'll judge it", and assert exactly that heading is reported. The active-requirement floor is raised from 135 to 264 in the spec test and from 137 to 264 in the hestia.rs test. docs/enforcement.md row M33 and CHANGELOG.md are updated. Spec test (30 passed), policy test and the hestia real-spec test pass. cargo fmt --all was run to fix formatting; clippy ran only on xtask; the full workspace test was not run.

open_issues: Roughly 60 of the new requirements have mechanism `none`, so the Hestia sweep will queue requests for them (five per pass, speed first). I used `none` where I could not confirm a real mechanism in the code. The owner should review whether any have one.

I confirmed a few mechanism names only from existing spec text and from files that exist: roles.rs, reading.rs, plan.rs, verify.rs, attribution.rs, manage.rs, `athena score-jev`. I did not open the code for each one. A verifier should spot-check them.
Some mechanism strings I wrote are partial: they name what exists and say what is missing, but are not `none`. The sweep will not queue those. Examples are OLY-B-A2-02, OLY-B-A5-04 and OLY-B-JDG-07.
OLY-B-O2-01 stays active although the 2026-10-17 note says Olympus replaces O2. I recorded this as OQ-10 and did not supersede it, since resolving it is out of scope.
Coverage counts only the first source of a requirement, as the earlier layers did. A heading cited only as a later source is reported as a gap, and a test covers this.
docs/decisions.md still describes the old coverage rule in older entries (D1xx, sections 1 to 5 and 7 to 10). I left them as history.
mistakes: I first wrote 129 as the count of new requirements in CHANGELOG.md; the real count is 127 and I corrected it after counting ids.
My first exempt-heading list in the test missed '9. Implementation plan', which has no text. The test failed and I fixed the list.
learnings: The headings with no text under them (title, Part 1/2/3, The operating model group, Addenda ×2, section 6, section 9) are exactly the ones the coverage rule exempts. The 'Addenda' heading appears twice in BRIEF.md.

Boundary-scan words appear in some brief headings: O5 'Restarts and the handoff boundary' and 'Running in this sandbox'. names_heading supports citing a heading by its start ending in '…', which these use. Quotes under those headings must avoid the banned words too.
crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs has its own floor on active requirements (was 137), separate from the spec test's floor (was 135).
docs/enforcement.md row M33 names spec tests that docs-policy (`every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists`) checks exist, so renaming a test needs that row updated.

Existing files that exist and can back mechanisms: docs/non-rust-files.md, docs/system-facts.md, docs/decisions.md, crates/athena-cap-study, crates/athena-cap-change, and `athena score-jev`, which the 2026-10-25 note names.
